construction: Replace all MNIST attention parameters by public pretrained; retain the exact frozen four-MLP release without new strength, fitting or compensation. Compare original, erasure-only, frozen-only and combined.
hypothesis: Removing a redundant task-update route might raise replacement cost while keeping utility; test the cheapest FC bypass before further attacks.
math: R_M R_A P_S(theta)=R_(M union A)(theta) when S is inside M. Removing attention task updates cannot restore their original values from the released attention alone; other modules and functional recovery may still bypass it.
selection: Target was chosen from previously inspected support ablations; this is adaptive development, not a fresh validation.
evaluation: Reuse inspected MNIST-4000 training confirmation and SVHN-1000 training development subsets. No official test labels or test selection.
fitting: No new fits, gradients, optimizer steps or calibration queries. Frozen protection retains its original 256-image calibration provenance.
early_stop: If utility loss exceeds 0.5 pp or any direct/zero-data replacement gap is below 5 pp, stop this construction and skip costly AGA/reconstruction. No retuning.
novelty: Task-vector sparsification and pretrained replacement are existing tools; not a novel algorithm or established defense. This checks redundancy removal as a possible support constraint.
